ebooks.title: Tulsidas
ebooks.subtitle: The Author of Ramcharitmanas
ebooks.description: The great poet-saint who wrote the Ramcharitmanas, retelling the Ramayana in Awadhi. His verses are recited in homes across North Bhārat.

ebooks.title: Anandamayi Ma
ebooks.subtitle: The Blissful Mother
ebooks.description: A 20th-century saint whose spontaneous spiritual ecstasy and unconditional love drew thousands to her. She taught through joyful presence rather than words.

ebooks.title: Sant Dnyaneshwar
ebooks.subtitle: The Young Sage
ebooks.description: A 13th-century Marathi saint who wrote the Dnyaneshwari, a commentary on the Bhagavad Gita. He became a saint at the age of 16.

ebooks.title: Narayana Guru
ebooks.subtitle: The Saint of Social Equality
ebooks.description: A spiritual leader from Kerala who challenged caste oppression and taught 'One Caste, One Religion, One God for All.' He built temples for all communities.

ebooks.title: Bahá'u'lláh
ebooks.subtitle: The Messenger of Unity
ebooks.description: The founder of the Baháʼí Faith, whose teachings on the unity of all religions, genders, and races inspired a global spiritual movement.

ebooks.title: Mahavatar Babaji
ebooks.subtitle: The Immortal Yogi
ebooks.description: A legendary Himalayan master believed to have lived for centuries. He initiated Kriya Yoga and appears in Yogananda's Autobiography of a Yogi as an immortal guide.

ebooks.title: Lao Tzu
ebooks.subtitle: The Ancient Eastern Philosopher
ebooks.description: The ancient Chinese philosopher and founder of Taoism, whose teachings on harmony, simplicity, and living in flow with nature influenced spiritual thought of Bhārat.

ebooks.title: Buddha
ebooks.subtitle: The Enlightened One
ebooks.description: Siddhartha Gautama, whose teachings of compassion, mindfulness, and the Middle Path transformed Asia. His message of peace continues to illuminate the world.

activities.title: Draw
activities.tagline: Bhārat has been drawing for 30,000 years — pick up a pencil and join the line.
activities.whatIs: Step-by-step drawing lessons, colouring sheets and art challenges inspired by Bhārat's painting traditions — from the murals of Ajanta to the folk art of today's villages.

knownFor.title: Madhubani
knownFor.text: Bihar's intricate line art, painted by Mithila women on walls and paper with natural colours — every peacock, fish and lotus carries a story.

knownFor.title: Warli
knownFor.text: Maharashtra's tribal art, where circles and triangles dance into villages, trees and festivals — made with just white paint and a stick.

knownFor.title: Pattachitra
knownFor.text: Odisha's scroll paintings, where artists still grind their own colours and paint gods and epics with one fine brush.

knownFor.title: Ajanta murals
knownFor.text: 1,600-year-old cave paintings so lifelike that artists still study them to learn how to draw a smile.

knownFor.title: Miniature paintings
knownFor.text: The tiny, jewel-bright court paintings of Rajasthan and the Himalayas — whole worlds of detail on a palm-sized page.

tryThis.title: Draw a Warli village
tryThis.text: Use only circles, triangles and squares. Draw a tree, a dancing family and a festival — all in white on brown paper, just like the Warli artists of Maharashtra.

activities.title: Make
activities.tagline: Fold, stick, tie and paint — crafts have kept Bhārat's festivals alive for centuries.
activities.whatIs: Hands-on craft projects inspired by Bhārat's festivals, toys and traditions — using paper, cloth, clay and things you can find in your kitchen.

knownFor.title: Channapatna toys
knownFor.text: Karnataka's wooden toys, coloured with natural lac — made for 200 years with no nails, no screws and no sharp edges.

knownFor.title: Kite-making
knownFor.text: Paper kites rule the skies of Uttarayan and Makar Sankranti — a craft that turns a sheet of paper into a flying festival.

knownFor.title: Rangoli
knownFor.text: Floor art of coloured powders, rice and petals, drawn at every doorstep to welcome guests and gods.

knownFor.title: Lanterns & torans
knownFor.text: Paper lanterns, flower garlands and door hangings that turn every home into a celebration of Bhārat.

knownFor.title: Patchwork & kantha
knownFor.text: Bengal's quilted storytelling — old saris stitched into warm, beautiful blankets of memory.

tryThis.title: Fold a paper boat
tryThis.text: The paper boat is Bhārat's favourite toy — it floats on every puddle after the rains. Fold one, write your name on it, and set it sailing. Then try a paper lantern for Diwali!

activities.title: Experiment
activities.tagline: Bhārat's scientists reached Mars and found water on the Moon — curiosity is our superpower.
activities.whatIs: Simple, safe experiments you can try at home, inspired by the discoveries that began on soil of Bhārat — from the number zero to the Mars mission.

knownFor.title: The zero
knownFor.text: Bhārat invented the number for 'nothing' — and every computer, rocket and equation on Earth stands on it.

knownFor.title: Aryabhata's spin
knownFor.text: A 5th-century astronomer proved the Earth rotates — a thousand years before Europe agreed.

knownFor.title: The rust-free pillar
knownFor.text: The Iron Pillar of Delhi has stood for 1,600 years without rusting — a chemistry mystery scientists still study.

knownFor.title: Sushruta's surgery
knownFor.text: Plastic surgery was performed in Bhārat 2,600 years ago — with 120 instruments and a student's oath.

knownFor.title: Mars on the first try
knownFor.text: ISRO reached Mars on its very first attempt — something no other space agency has managed.

tryThis.title: The spinning Earth
tryThis.text: Draw a dot on a table-tennis ball. Spin it slowly — see how the dot faces you, then turns away. That's exactly why the Sun seems to rise and set: the Earth spins, just as Aryabhata said 1,500 years ago.

activities.title: Build
activities.tagline: From 4,500-year-old cities to Moon landers — Bhārat builds big.
activities.whatIs: Build models, machines and structures and think like an engineer — in the footsteps of the builders of Dholavira, the stepwells and ISRO.

knownFor.title: Dholavira
knownFor.text: A 4,500-year-old Harappan city with the world's first signboard — planned streets, water tanks and all.

knownFor.title: The stepwells
knownFor.text: The baolis of Gujarat and Rajasthan are giant reverse towers — engineering that brings water up from deep underground.

knownFor.title: The Taj Mahal
knownFor.text: Built 370 years ago with no computers — perfectly balanced, down to the last millimetre.

knownFor.title: Jantar Mantar
knownFor.text: Jaipur's stone observatories are buildings that tell the time and track the stars.

knownFor.title: ISRO rockets
knownFor.text: Bhārat's space rockets began as parts carried on bicycles — and now land on the Moon.

tryThis.title: Build a paper bridge
tryThis.text: Roll five sheets of paper into tight tubes. Tape them side by side across two books — then test how many books your bridge can hold. That's real civil engineering!

activities.title: Write
activities.tagline: Bhārat told the world's most-loved stories — now it's your turn to add one.
activities.whatIs: Stories, poems, comics and letters — with prompts inspired by the tales that have travelled from Bhārat to every corner of the world.

knownFor.title: Panchatantra
knownFor.text: Animal fables written 2,000 years ago to teach wisdom — now told in more than 50 languages across the planet.

knownFor.title: Jataka tales
knownFor.text: The past-life stories of the Buddha — the source of folktales told from Persia to Europe.

knownFor.title: The great epics
knownFor.text: The Ramayana and Mahabharata — among the longest and greatest poems ever written.

knownFor.title: Akbar–Birbal riddles
knownFor.text: Riddle tales of the clever minister who out-thought everyone — Bhārat's favourite brain-teaser stories.

knownFor.title: Tagore's Gitanjali
knownFor.text: Rabindranath Tagore's poems won the Nobel Prize — the first Asian writer to do so.

tryThis.title: Write a Panchatantra fable
tryThis.text: Pick two animals (a clever fox and a slow tortoise?), give them one problem, and end with a lesson. Two hundred words is plenty — that's how the world's fables began.

activities.title: Make Your Own Newspaper
activities.tagline: Newspapers helped win Bhārat's freedom — now print your own edition!
activities.whatIs: Design and publish your very own newspaper — headline, news, cartoons and ads — like the brave papers that spoke for Bhārat.

knownFor.title: Bengal Gazette
knownFor.text: Bhārat's first newspaper, printed in 1780 in Kolkata — written by hand, printed by machine.

knownFor.title: Kesari
knownFor.text: Bal Gangadhar Tilak's fiery paper that woke a nation — and taught people of Bhārat their own history.

knownFor.title: The Hindu
knownFor.text: Born in 1878 to fight an unfair tax, still published every single day from Chennai.

knownFor.title: The voice of freedom
knownFor.text: From Swadeshi to Satyagraha, newspapers carried the freedom movement into every home.

knownFor.title: Radio & beyond
knownFor.text: When villages had no papers, radio told the news in every language of Bhārat.

tryThis.title: Publish a one-page paper
tryThis.text: Give it a name (like 'Pakka Patriot Junior'), write one headline about your week, two short news items, a cartoon, and one ad for your favourite mithai. Print it or copy it for your family!

activities.title: Create Videos
activities.tagline: Bhārat makes more films than any country on Earth — roll your own 60 seconds!
activities.whatIs: Make 60-second videos — stories, talents and ideas — in the land that built a cinema loved across the planet.

knownFor.title: Raja Harishchandra
knownFor.text: In 1913, Dadasaheb Phalke made Bhārat's first film — a silent epic shot entirely in Bhārat.

knownFor.title: Mythological epics
knownFor.text: The Ramayana and Mahabharata serials brought whole families to their televisions — and made history.

knownFor.title: RRR & Baahubali
knownFor.text: films now smash of Bhārat records from Japan to America — a billion fans and counting.

knownFor.title: Oscars & Cannes
knownFor.text: From Satyajit Ray to 'Naatu Naatu', cinema of Bhārat keeps winning the world's top awards.

knownFor.title: Animation for kids
knownFor.text: Chhota Bheem and friends — cartoons loved by children of Bhārat across the globe.

tryThis.title: Make a silent film
tryThis.text: Shoot 60 seconds with no dialogue — only actions, music and expression. Bhārat's first film had no sound at all — and it conquered the country!

activities.title: My Bhārat
activities.tagline: Snow peaks, tiger forests, temple towns — your Bhārat is worth photographing.
activities.whatIs: Upload photos of your place and show the world the beauty around you — every lane, field and sky of Bhārat is a story.

knownFor.title: Mountains to beaches
knownFor.text: From the snowy Himalayas to coconut-fringed shores — Bhārat holds every kind of beauty on Earth.

knownFor.title: Wild wonders
knownFor.text: Bengal tigers, one-horned rhinos and dancing peacocks — Bhārat protects more wildlife than most nations.

knownFor.title: Ancient marvels
knownFor.text: The Taj Mahal, Hampi, Khajuraho — wonder after wonder, built thousands of years apart.

knownFor.title: Festivals in every field
knownFor.text: Every region celebrates its own harvests, music and colours — a different Bhārat around every corner.

knownFor.title: The everyday
knownFor.text: A chai stall, a rangoli doorstep, a kite on a roof — Bhārat's real beauty is in its everyday.

tryThis.title: Photo-walk your street
tryThis.text: Take 5 photos of your neighbourhood — a shop, a tree, a building, a pet, a sky. Write one line under each. That's your My Bhārat exhibition!

activities.title: Make a Game
activities.tagline: Chess, Snakes & Ladders and Pachisi all began in Bhārat — design the next one!
activities.whatIs: Design your own board game — theme, rules, dice and challenges — following the ancient game-makers of Bhārat.

knownFor.title: Moksha Patam
knownFor.text: The original Snakes & Ladders — a lesson of Bhārat in karma, where ladders lifted virtue and snakes dragged down vice.

knownFor.title: Chaturanga
knownFor.text: The war game that became chess — born in Bhārat 1,500 years ago.

knownFor.title: Pachisi
knownFor.text: The royal cross-board game of the Mahabharata, played by kings and queens.

knownFor.title: Chaukabaara
knownFor.text: Cowrie-shell racing on a square board — 2,000 years old and still played in villages.

knownFor.title: Aadu Puli Aatam
knownFor.text: Goats versus tigers on a temple triangle — a South Bhārat classic of pure strategy.

tryThis.title: Design a 20-square board
tryThis.text: Pick a theme (samosas vs jalebis?), draw 20 squares, write 3 rules, add 2 shortcuts and 2 traps. Now play it with your family — and improve it!

activities.title: Puzzles & Printables
activities.tagline: Bhārat built the first magic squares — and the best puzzles still come from here.
activities.whatIs: Crosswords, mazes, colouring sheets and maths puzzles — downloadable and printable, inspired by Bhārat's number-wizards.

knownFor.title: Magic squares
knownFor.text: A 1,000-year-old temple in Bhārat hides a 4×4 magic square — every row, column and diagonal adds up to 34.

knownFor.title: Ramanujan's 1729
knownFor.text: The taxi number! 1729 is the smallest number you can write as two cubes in two different ways — Ramanujan knew it instantly.

knownFor.title: Vedic maths
knownFor.text: Lightning-fast mental arithmetic tricks, written in the Vedas thousands of years ago.

knownFor.title: The decimal system
knownFor.text: Bhārat's place-value system turned arithmetic into a game anyone can win.

knownFor.title: Maps & mazes
knownFor.text: Puzzle-makers have turned Bhārat's geography into mazes, jigsaws and dot-to-dots for kids everywhere.

tryThis.title: Prove 1729
tryThis.text: Find two different pairs of cubes that add up to the same number. Hint: 1³ + 12³ = 9³ + 10³ — that's 1 + 1728 = 729 + 1000 = 1729!

activities.title: Create with Grandparents
activities.tagline: Every grandparent carries a library of stories — record yours before it's too late.
activities.whatIs: Ask, record and preserve the stories, songs and wisdom of your grandparents — Bhārat's greatest unwritten treasure.

knownFor.title: Grandma's tales
knownFor.text: Every family has a thousand stories of Bhārat — of journeys, festivals, mischief and miracles.

knownFor.title: Lullabies
knownFor.text: The first songs a child of Bhārat hears are grandmother songs — passed down for generations.

knownFor.title: Proverbs & riddles
knownFor.text: A whole philosophy in one sentence — every language has its own wise sayings of Bhārat.

knownFor.title: Nani's kitchen
knownFor.text: Home remedies for every cough and cut — a living pharmacy of grandma's recipes.

knownFor.title: Festival customs
knownFor.text: Grandparents are the keepers of how we light lamps, tie rakhis and make sweets.

tryThis.title: Interview a grandparent
tryThis.text: Record 5 questions: What was your childhood? Your first festival memory? Your school? One brave moment? One piece of advice? Keep the recording — it will be priceless.

activities.title: Create for Bhārat
activities.tagline: The future of Bhārat will be built by kids like you — start today.
activities.whatIs: Take challenges and create ideas that make Bhārat better — cleaner, greener, kinder and smarter.

knownFor.title: Space for everyone
knownFor.text: Dr. Sarabhai believed rockets should serve farmers and schools — and today they do.

knownFor.title: Swachh Bharat
knownFor.text: A nationwide mission that built millions of toilets and cleaned thousands of towns.

knownFor.title: Kid innovators
knownFor.text: School children have invented solar lamps, sanitary machines and low-cost tractors — some of the world's best ideas come from kids.

knownFor.title: Chipko hugging
knownFor.text: Villagers hugged trees to save their forests — a hug that changed Bhārat's laws.

knownFor.title: Ideas that unite
knownFor.text: From the Constitution to the tricolour, Bhārat was built by big, bold ideas.

tryThis.title: Spot a problem, sketch a fix
tryThis.text: Look around your neighbourhood. Pick one small problem (wasted water? plastic on the street?) and sketch 3 ideas to solve it. One of them could be the next big invention of Bhārat!
